content: For infants under 30 days of age, the recommended treatment for congenital syphilis includes ceftriaxone administered at a dose of 75 mg per kilogram of body weight, either intramuscularly (IM) or intravenously (IV), once daily for 10 to 14 days. For infants aged 30 days or older, the dosage increases to 100 mg per kilogram of body weight, administered in the same manner and for the same duration. In cases where infants are clinically normal but their mothers had untreated syphilis, inadequately treated syphilis, or syphilis treated with non-penicillin regimens, the treatment options include benzyl penicillin at a dose of 100,000 to 150,000 units per kilogram per day for 10 to 15 days, procaine penicillin at 50,000 units per kilogram per day for 10 to 15 days, or a single dose of benzathine penicillin at 50,000 units per kilogram administered intramuscularly. Ceftriaxone may also be used as an alternative, with the same dosing regimens as described above for infants under and over 30 days of age. For infants who are clinically normal and whose mothers had adequately treated syphilis with no signs of reinfection, the recommended course of action is either no treatment or a single dose of benzathine penicillin at 50,000 units per kilogram administered intramuscularly. Alternatively, ceftriaxone may be administered as a single dose, with the dosage adjusted based on the infant's age (75 mg/kg for those under 30 days and 100 mg/kg for those 30 days or older). The critical outcomes for these treatment regimens include achieving clinical cure, ensuring a serologic response, and addressing any manifestations of congenital syphilis.
